title: CSRF Protection in ASP.NET Core
description: Implement antiforgery tokens and validate requests in .NET APIs.

data.text: ASP.NET Core includes built-in antiforgery support. The server generates a token, the client sends it back, and the server validates it.

items: Server generates two tokens: a cookie token and a request token
The cookie token is sent automatically
The request token must be provided by the client (header or form field)
Server validates both tokens match before processing

data.text: Read the cookie and attach it as a header for state-changing requests.

data.title: SameSite Cookies
data.text: Set cookie SameSite=Strict or Lax to reduce CSRF risk further.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Antiforgery uses a cookie token + request token
React reads the cookie and sends a header
ASP.NET Core validates both tokens automatically
Combine with SameSite cookies for defense in depth
data.takeaway: Next, we'll secure the React side against XSS.
